ops.title: csops_audittoken reads a suspended, unreleased child's full code identity (macOS 26.5.2)
ops.body:
Measured 2026-08-01, macOS 26.5.2 (25F84, arm64), by the P4.1 F1b spike. The question was whether a
Go parent can verify the code identity of a child it has spawned but not yet released, under the
hardened runtime — the whole `Cmd.Exec` fix for [[spawned-lane-authenticates-nothing]] depended on
the answer.

**PASS.** The entire shipping `trust.Verify` — all six csops ops, CMS chain, DER entitlements —
succeeds against a child that has not executed a single instruction.

Binding mechanics that came out of the spike and are now design directives:

- **Token source:** `task_name_for_pid` + `TASK_AUDIT_TOKEN`, not a synthesized token.
- **Gate shape:** the check returns an error into the existing `abortSpawn` path. It must NOT kill in
  a void hook — the spike found that shape produces a live-looking exit 137.
- **It verifies the child in place**, never a staged copy: App Group entitlements derive from the
  launched bundle path (P4.0 binding constraint 1).
- **TOCTOU-free by construction:** a child we spawned and have not reaped cannot have its pid
  recycled.
- **Cost:** ~6% of spawn.
- **Gap:** CI lacks the `.trust-fixtures` this exercises; the signed-peer fixture lane still has no
  CI home.
